senses.gloss: A person who takes advantage of others in a harmful way, especially sexually or financially.
examples: The article described him as a *predator* who targeted teenage girls.
Payday lenders have been called financial *predators*.
Parents worry about online *predators* in gaming chats.

senses.gloss: Harm to someone's rights or legal position, especially in the phrases with prejudice and without prejudice.
examples: The judge dismissed the case with *prejudice*, so it can never be refiled.
She resigned without *prejudice* to her right to sue later.
The two-year delay caused real *prejudice* to the defense.

senses.gloss: A substance mixed or made up for a particular use, such as a medicine or a cosmetic.
examples: The pharmacist recommended an over-the-counter *preparation* for the itching.
This *preparation* has to be refrigerated after it is opened.
Some herbal *preparations* interact badly with prescription drugs.

senses.gloss: A recommended course of action for fixing a problem.
examples: His *prescription* for the economy is lower taxes and less regulation.
The report is long on diagnosis and short on *prescriptions*.
Cutting the budget that fast is a *prescription* for disaster.

senses.gloss: The way something is arranged and offered to be looked at.
examples: The food tasted fine, but the *presentation* was sloppy.
Judges score the cakes on flavor and on *presentation*.
A little parsley improves the *presentation* of the dish.

senses.gloss: Fruit cooked with sugar and sealed in jars, chunkier than jelly.
examples: She spread strawberry *preserves* on her toast.
The farm stand sells honey and homemade *preserves*.
We put up six jars of peach *preserves* every August.

senses.gloss: An activity or area treated as belonging to one group alone.
examples: Coding was once the *preserve* of a few specialists.
The club stayed the *preserve* of a handful of old families.
Space flight is no longer the sole *preserve* of governments.

senses.gloss: The person who heads a company, bank, university, or other organization.
examples: She was named *president* of the bank last spring.
The college *president* sent an email to every student.
Both *presidents* of the union locals spoke at the rally.

senses.gloss: A room set aside at an event or a building for reporters to work in.
examples: Reporters filed their stories from the *pressroom* in the basement.
The coach came into the *pressroom* twenty minutes after the game.
Only credentialed journalists are allowed in the *pressroom*.

senses.gloss: The person in charge of a school.
examples: The *principal* called my parents about the fight.
She has been the *principal* at Lincoln Elementary for nine years.
Two *principals* from the district came to the board meeting.

senses.gloss: Handwriting made with separate letters instead of joined cursive.
examples: Please use *printing*, not cursive, on the form.
His *printing* is much neater than his signature.
First graders are graded on their *printing*.

senses.gloss: All the copies of a book produced at one time.
examples: The novel is already in its fourth *printing*.
The first *printing* sold out in a week.
Later *printings* fixed the typo on page thirty.

senses.gloss: A medical operation or treatment.
examples: She is having a minor *procedure* on Thursday.
The *procedure* takes an hour and needs no overnight stay.
Insurance covers most outpatient *procedures*.

senses.gloss: A company or plant that treats raw material or handles transactions in bulk.
examples: The country's largest meat *processor* recalled a million pounds of beef.
Our payment *processor* charges three percent on every sale.
Local growers sell to a tomato *processor* in the next county.

senses.gloss: A person, company, or country that grows or makes something.
examples: Iowa is the top corn *producer* in the country.
Small dairy *producers* are being squeezed out by the big ones.
The firm is the world's largest *producer* of lithium batteries.

senses.gloss: A play, opera, or show as it is staged and performed.
examples: The theater's new *production* runs through May.
Her first Broadway *production* closed after eleven performances.
It is a modern *production* set in a subway station.

senses.gloss: An open statement of a belief or feeling, often one that others doubt.
examples: His *professions* of innocence convinced no one on the jury.
She made a public *profession* of faith at the church.
The letter was full of *professions* of loyalty.

senses.gloss: The verb form ending in -ing, used for an action that is going on.
examples: Use the present *progressive* for something happening right now.
Stative verbs are rarely used in the *progressive*.
The past *progressive* sets the scene for another event.

senses.gloss: An estimate of what a number will be at some future point.
examples: Sales fell well short of the company's *projections*.
The budget rests on a *projection* of three percent growth.
Early *projections* gave her a narrow lead.

senses.gloss: The habit of seeing your own unwanted feelings in other people instead.
examples: Calling everyone else lazy sounds like *projection* to me.
The therapist explained *projection* with a simple example.
That accusation is pure *projection*.

senses.gloss: A special offer or campaign used to sell something.
examples: The store is running a two-for-one *promotion* this week.
Free shipping is just a holiday *promotion*.
The team ran a bobblehead *promotion* to fill the seats.

senses.gloss: The spreading of something such as a wave, a signal, or an idea.
examples: Hills interfere with the *propagation* of radio signals.
Social media speeds the *propagation* of rumors.
The *propagation* of sound is slower in cold air.

senses.gloss: A quality or characteristic that belongs to a substance or a thing.
examples: Aloe is said to have healing *properties*.
Heat changes the chemical *properties* of the metal.
One useful *property* of salt is that it melts ice.

senses.gloss: An offer of marriage.
examples: He planned the *proposal* for months.
She said yes about ten seconds into the *proposal*.
The whole restaurant clapped after the *proposal*.

senses.gloss: A measure put directly to voters on a ballot.
examples: The *proposition* to raise the sales tax failed by six points.
There are five *propositions* on the November ballot.
Voters approved the school bond *proposition*.

senses.gloss: A young player expected to become very good.
examples: He was the team's top pitching *prospect* two years ago.
Scouts rank her among the best *prospects* in the state.
The trade brought back two *prospects* and a draft pick.

senses.gloss: A doctor, nurse, or clinic that gives medical care.
examples: Check that the clinic is in your network before choosing a *provider*.
Your primary care *provider* can refer you to a specialist.
Rural counties keep losing health care *providers*.

senses.gloss: Someone who earns the money that supports a family.
examples: He was a steady *provider* who never missed a day of work.
After the layoff she became the family's only *provider*.
In their parents' generation the husband was expected to be the *provider*.

senses.gloss: Food and other supplies gathered for a trip or a stay.
examples: We loaded the canoe with *provisions* for five days.
The lighthouse keeper got *provisions* once a month.
They ran short of *provisions* halfway through the trek.

senses.gloss: The act of supplying something that people need.
examples: The law deals with the *provision* of clean drinking water.
The city is responsible for the *provision* of trash collection.
Federal money covers the *provision* of free school lunches.

senses.gloss: The way a particular person or group thinks and reacts.
examples: You have to understand the *psychology* of a hungry crowd.
Coaches spend as much time on *psychology* as on drills.
Reverse *psychology* never works on my kids.

senses.gloss: Rough treatment or hard wear that something has to stand.
examples: These boots can take a lot of *punishment*.
The old truck took real *punishment* on the logging roads.
His knees have absorbed years of *punishment* from running.

senses.gloss: A firm grip or foothold that keeps something from slipping.
examples: The ladder could not get any *purchase* on the icy step.
He grabbed the branch, lost his *purchase*, and slid down.
New tires give the truck better *purchase* in mud.

senses.gloss: A miserable state of waiting or suffering that seems to have no end.
examples: We spent four hours in airport *purgatory* waiting out the storm.
The bill sat in committee *purgatory* for two years.
Being on hold with the insurance company is my idea of *purgatory*.

senses.gloss: A word or remark added to limit what has just been said.
examples: He agreed, but with the *qualifier* that the price could change.
Words like usually and mostly are *qualifiers*.
Notice the *qualifier* in her answer: she said probably.

senses.gloss: A matter or issue that is being discussed or decided.
examples: The *question* of funding was left for the next meeting.
Whether the law applies here is an open *question*.
That brings us to the *question* of who pays for repairs.

senses.gloss: A stated price for a job or for goods.
examples: We got three *quotations* before hiring a roofer.
The contractor's *quotation* came in under budget.
Ask for a written *quotation* rather than a verbal estimate.
